D018-D005_h001.question: "It's just... I can't shake it. Every time I hear a sudden loud bang, like a pot dropping in the kitchen, my heart races and I practically jump out of my skin. It's like I'm back in that moment all over again. I find myself replaying what happened, and I keep thinking about what I could have done differently, how it’s my fault. I don't feel happy anymore, even when I'm baking my favorite recipes; nothing gives me joy like it used to. I don't know, it just feels like this constant anger boiling beneath the surface. And the hallucinations… sometimes I see flashes, like quick replays of the event, and I hear things connected to it. It’s always about what happened, never anything else weird. It's hard to focus in class, too, my mind just drifts, and I can't concentrate on lectures or recipes. It's been like this for over two months now."
D018-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h002.question:
It's been almost eight months since the accident, and things just haven't been right. I'm constantly on edge. The smallest thing, like a siren wailing past, can send me spiraling back into that night. I see the flashing lights, hear the screams, and it's like I'm right there again, my heart pounding out of my chest, struggling to breathe.

I used to love my job, the camaraderie, the feeling of helping people, but now? I don't feel much of anything positive. Happiness, satisfaction – they're just words. I keep replaying it in my head, thinking if the other driver had just been more careful, none of this would have happened. It makes me so angry, a constant simmering rage under the surface that sometimes boils over at the smallest provocation.

My memory is shot. I forget why I walked into a room or where I put my keys half the time, probably because my mind is always somewhere else. And any sudden loud noise, like a dropped plate, makes me jump out of my skin. There are times I hear things, whispers from that night, but it’s always about the accident, those desperate calls for help. I’ve never heard anything else, no strange voices telling me to do things, just echoes of that night.
D018-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h003.question:
It's getting harder to focus, doc. My mind feels foggy, like a perpetual haze that just won't lift. I’m just not myself anymore. Ever since the accident at the plant, I can't shake the images of the scaffolding collapsing. They just... pop into my head. Over and over, clear as day, even when I'm trying to weld. It’s like I’m reliving it.

And the touch. My wife, bless her heart, tries to comfort me, but if she so much as lays a hand on me unexpectedly, I jump out of my skin. It’s just too much. I keep thinking, if only I’d double-checked that weld, maybe it wouldn't have happened. The shame of it all, it just eats at me. Everything feels grey. I used to enjoy working with my hands, coming home, spending time with my wife, but now? There’s no joy in anything. Sometimes I even see the beams falling, right there in front of me, but it's always the accident. Always that moment. It's like my mind is stuck in that loop. Aside from that, I am otherwise well.
D018-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h004.question: It’s been almost seven months since the fire at the restaurant, and I just can't shake it. I keep seeing the flames, smelling the smoke, and hearing the screams – it all replays in my mind repeatedly, like a horrific movie I’m being forced to watch. It’s not just memories; sometimes it feels so real, like it’s happening right now, even when I know it’s not, and it’s always about that night. It’s hard to care about things anymore; running the restaurant used to be my passion, but now even thinking about ordering supplies or planning menus feels like too much effort. Everything is a chore. I find myself constantly thinking about who was responsible, pointing fingers at the faulty wiring I complained about or the delayed emergency response. How could this have happened? The horror of that night just doesn't fade; it’s like a permanent knot in my stomach. Even small decisions, like what to wear, feel impossible to make. And if there’s a sudden noise, my heart races, I start trembling, and it takes ages for me to calm down. It’s exhausting.
D018-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h005.question:
I'm here because things have been really tough lately, going on for about eight months now. Ever since that car accident, sleep has been a nightmare; almost every night, I’m back in that moment, reliving the crash in my dreams. When I'm awake, it's not much better. I keep replaying it in my head, and sometimes it's like I'm right there again, seeing and hearing it all unfold, even though I know I'm in my living room. I just can't shake the feeling that it was my fault, that I should have done something differently. The guilt is a constant weight, draining all the joy out of life. Nothing feels good anymore, not even spending time with my husband or my old hobbies.

My memory feels shot, too. I used to be so organized at work, but now I'm constantly forgetting where I put my keys or important documents. And I'm always on edge. The slightest sudden noise, like a door slamming or a car horn, makes me jump out of my skin. It's like I'm constantly bracing for impact, even when nothing's there.
D018-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h006.question:
It's been almost eight months since the accident at work, the one with the multi-car pile-up victims. I feel like I'm constantly on edge. Even the smell of antiseptic or the sound of sirens makes my heart race and my palms sweat, like I'm right back there. I try so hard not to think about it, to push all those awful images out of my head, but it's like a broken record.

And then there are these… moments. Sometimes, I’ll swear I can see the victim with the head injury, right there in front of me, like they're still alive and looking at me with those vacant eyes. It’s so vivid, like it's happening all over again. It’s always about the accident, though, never anything else. It's not like I'm hearing voices telling me things or thinking people are out to get me, it’s just that one terrifying memory playing on a loop. Most of the time, I just feel numb, like I'm watching my own life from a distance. Nothing makes me happy anymore. My nerves are completely shot; the slightest thing can set me off. If someone moves too quickly near me, I jump out of my skin, always ready to snap. It's exhausting.
D018-D005_h006.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h007.question:
"Lately, it's just… a lot. I'm a wedding photographer, so I'm supposed to capture joy, but it feels like there's a dark cloud following me. It's been about eight months since the accident. I can't really remember much of it, just bits and pieces. What I do remember, though, keeps coming back. Sometimes I'll be editing photos, and suddenly I’m right back there, feeling the impact, hearing the screams – it’s like it’s happening all over again, even though I know it's not. I try so hard not to think about it, to push it away, but it’s always there, lurking.

My husband tries to be understanding, but I feel so distant from him, and even from my family. It’s like I'm numb to the love they’re offering. And my temper… it’s awful. The other day, a car just swerved a little too close on the road, and I just *exploded* with road rage, screaming. Or if someone comes up behind me too quickly, I jump out of my skin. It’s getting hard to live like this. The visions, they're always about *that day*, and it's just those visions, nothing else. I don't feel crazy; it's like my mind just won't let go of what happened."
D018-D005_h007.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h008.question:
It’s hard to pinpoint when things really started, but I’ve been feeling off for at least six months now, ever since that assignment overseas. I keep having these graphic dreams, not just scary, but about *that day*—the smells, the sounds, everything. When I’m awake, I try so hard not to think about it, to push all those awful memories away. But then something triggers me, and it’s like I’m right back there, seeing things, hearing things that aren’t here. They're always about the incident, never anything else random. My heart starts pounding, and I can literally feel myself shaking for ages afterward, long after whatever startled me is done.

It’s made me feel so disconnected. I just can’t feel love anymore, not for my family, not for anyone. It’s like that part of me has shut down. There are parts of that day I just can’t recall, like my mind decided to redact certain sections, even though other parts are crystal clear. And my fuse is so short now. I snap, I shout, I say things I instantly regret, but in the moment, it just flies out without me being able to stop it. It’s like I’m constantly on edge.
D018-D005_h008.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h009.question:
Lately, I just feel… empty. It’s like a cloud has settled over everything good. I try to teach my Pilates classes, but my mind is constantly elsewhere, drifting to *that day*. Then, out of nowhere, I'm back there, truly feeling like it's happening all over again. Sometimes I’ll snap out of it and realize I’ve been staring blankly, completely zoned out from my class. I try so hard not to think about it, to push all those awful memories away. The strange thing is, I can’t even remember most of what happened during the incident itself, it’s all just a blank.

I’m so on edge. If someone walks up behind me quickly, even one of my students, I jump right out of my skin. And my temper… it’s frightening. The other day, my ex-husband said something dismissive about my schedule, and I just lost it, throwing a water bottle across the room. I’ve even started seeing things, glimpses of him, the attacker, always in the periphery. They are terrifying because they make me feel like I’m right back in that moment. There's no other strange stuff happening, no other voices, just him, and it's always tied to *that*.
D018-D005_h009.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h010.question: It’s been almost seven months since the incident, and I just can't shake it. I keep seeing his face, you know? Sometimes, I’ll be on a call, and suddenly, I’m back in that alley, the screams, the blood… it’s like I’m reliving it. And then I lash out, throwing my coffee mug, yelling at my wife. Afterwards, my heart pounds for what feels like hours. I try to avoid going near that part of town, or even talking about that case, but it doesn’t help. It's like a part of my memory from that night is just… gone, faded, but the worst parts are crystal clear. Even when I close a tough case now, there's no relief, no real satisfaction. It's just… empty. These "visions" are always about that night. It's not like I'm hearing voices or anything else strange unconnected to what happened; it's just that moment, over and over.
D018-D005_h010.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h011.question:
It’s been almost a year since the accident at the festival, and things just aren't right. I'm 29, single, and used to love my work as a sound engineer, but now it feels like a chore. I’ll be mixing a track, and suddenly, I’m back there, the stage collapsing, the screams. It’s like I’m reliving it – the dust, the sounds – like it’s happening again in my studio. It's so vivid sometimes it feels real, like I can hear the debris and the cries for help. I’ve started avoiding live shows, even just walking past venues. It stirs everything up, and I just can't deal with it.

I feel like the world is just completely dangerous now. Before, I was outgoing, but now I’m convinced there's a threat lurking everywhere. And honestly, I can't help but blame the venue management. They cut corners, I know it, and that’s why all of this happened. It’s just so frustrating. Sometimes, I just snap at people, yelling and cursing, especially if they try to tell me to "get over it." It's like I lose control of my temper.
D018-D005_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h012.question:
It’s been about eight months since the accident, and honestly, things just haven’t been normal. I'm a university admissions officer, so I'm usually pretty organized and good with people, but now… it's a mess. I keep having these moments where I feel like I'm right back there, seeing and hearing everything as if it's happening all over again – it’s like a movie playing in my head that I can’t turn off. I try to stay away from the part of town where it happened, and even just talking about it or anything that reminds me of it sends me into a tailspin.

My wife says I've changed. I push people away sometimes. I just can’t help feeling like the world is a dangerous place and you can't trust anyone. I even blame myself, thinking I should have done something differently, even though logically I know it wasn't my fault. And sometimes, when these flashbacks hit, I get so overwhelmed I just lash out. I've thrown things, even nearly punched a wall. It’s not like me at all. I know these visions I have are just reliving that night, not seeing things that aren't there, and it's always just that one event, nothing else.
D018-D005_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h013.question:
It's been close to seven months now since the—incident. I can't stop thinking about it, no matter how hard I try. I try to keep my mind blank, or throw myself into work, scrubbing away everything. But a certain smell, or even just the sight of a familiar street, and my heart starts pounding, sweat dripping down my back like I'm right there again. Sometimes, it's like I’m seeing it all happen as if it’s real, right in front of my eyes, even when I know it’s just the memory playing tricks.

I find myself snapping at people, sometimes even throwing things in frustration. It's not like me. I feel like the world is just a dangerous place, and there’s no point to anything anymore. If I had just done something differently, maybe… I just keep replaying it, blaming myself over and over. These visions, they always bring me back to that day, like a broken record in my head.
D018-D005_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h014.question: It’s been almost a year since the accident, and I just can't shake it. Every time I hear screeching tires, my heart pounds out of my chest, and I get all sweaty, just like it’s happening again. I try so hard not to think about it, to push all the awful memories and feelings away, but they just… resurface. I know it sounds crazy, but sometimes I even see flashes of the wreck, like it's unfolding right in front of me, even when I'm wide awake. It's like a movie playing in my head, and I can't turn it off. I keep telling myself that the world is a dangerous place, and that there’s no real point to anything anymore. And the worst part is, I often blame myself. If only I’d left a minute earlier, or taken a different route. This anger just builds up in me, and sometimes it just boils over. I’ve yelled at my husband and even thrown things across the room. It’s not like me at all.
D018-D005_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h015.question:
“It’s been almost a year since my husband, bless his soul, passed during that home invasion. I can still see it, clear as day. It just… flashes into my mind, involuntary, over and over, especially when I’m trying to relax. I try so hard to push those thoughts away, to not think about what happened, but it’s like living through it again and again. Sometimes, I hear his voice, or what I imagine is his voice, calling out, almost like he’s still there. It’s not like those crazy voices you read about in books, though; it’s always about that night, replaying in my head.

I just feel like the world is a dangerous place now, completely different from how I used to see it. And if only I had just locked that back door, maybe none of this would have happened. I keep blaming myself. I’ve become so irritable, too. My daughter-in-law, bless her heart, tries to help, but I just snap at her, screaming and feeling awful afterward. I never used to be like this. It’s always been peaceful in our home, even after retirement, but not anymore.”
D018-D005_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h016.question:
It’s been rough, doc. Ever since that incident a few months back – a passenger jumped in front of my train – I haven't been right. I keep seeing it, you know? Not just in my mind, but sometimes it feels like he's there on the tracks, right in front of me, even when I'm just sitting at home. These aren't like voices talking to me or anything; it's always him, that moment, replaying itself. It makes me jump, my heart pounding, even when I know it's not real. I try my best to push those thoughts away, to distract myself, but they just… force their way in.

I can’t help but think about the shift supervisor who insisted I stick to the schedule, even though I felt a bit off that morning. It feels like if he had just been a bit more understanding, maybe it wouldn't have happened. Now, every single time I’m at work, or even just out and about, I’m constantly looking around, checking every shadow, every person, like something bad is about to happen again. It's exhausting, this constant state of alert.
D018-D005_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h017.question:
It’s been over a year now since that night, and things just aren't right. I try to keep it together, especially with my job, but it’s getting harder. I find myself constantly scanning rooms, checking exits, and watching everyone around me. It's like I'm always on high alert, even when I'm just getting groceries. I avoid certain streets, certain types of cars, even certain noises if they remind me too much of what happened. If I hear anything that sounds like a gunshot, or even a firecracker, my heart just pounds and it feels like I'm right back there.

And the voices… they're not like in the movies, just disembodied. It's more like I hear fragments of what was said that night, what *I* said, almost like a replay. It’s always about the incident, never anything else random. I keep replaying moments in my head, convinced I could have done something different. I blame myself, you know? If I had just reacted faster, or been more careful… I know it sounds crazy, having these things pop up, but it's only ever when I'm thinking about it, or something triggers a memory of that night. It’s not like I’m seeing things that aren't there or believing bizarre stuff. It’s always about *that*.
D018-D005_h017.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h018.question: "Lately, it's just been a constant replay in my head, sir. That night at the warehouse, it comes back in jagged flashes, even when I'm just trying to have dinner with my wife. I try to push it away, you know? The sounds, the fear… I just want to forget it. It’s like a movie playing, and I’m forced to watch it, hearing the yelling, seeing the chaos. It’s always there, even when I'm wide awake. I find myself constantly looking over my shoulder, even here in your office, assessing every person, every corner. I keep thinking, 'What if something happens again?' And as for what happened, I keep thinking about my supervisor. He should have had better security measures in place. He’s the one who really dropped the ball, putting us all at risk that night. It’s not fair that I’m the one suffering like this when he’s the one who was truly negligent."
D018-D005_h018.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h019.question: It’s been almost seven months since the accident at the hospital, the one where that drunk driver plowed through the ER entrance. I can still see the mangled car, hear the screams. Even when I'm trying to relax, flashes of it just pop into my head, completely out of nowhere, and it's like I'm back there. It’s hard to even pass by the hospital now, let alone work there, I try to take different routes, anything to avoid the street where it happened. I find myself constantly looking around, checking the exits in every room I enter, making sure I know where to go if something happens again. I keep replaying the incident, honestly, I blame the security guard who was supposed to be on duty that night. If he had been more vigilant, maybe this wouldn’t have happened. The weirdest part is, sometimes I even see it unfolding right in front of me, like I’m reliving it, but it's just in my head, a replay of the trauma, and nothing else feels off, just this persistent loop.
D018-D005_h019.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h020.question: It's been almost six months now since everything happened, and I just can't seem to get it out of my head. I try to push those thoughts away, try to distract myself, but they just… come back. I keep replaying it, trying to figure out what I could have done differently, how I could have stopped it. I just keep blaming myself for what happened. It messes with my head so much that sometimes I hear things directly from that day, like the shouts and the sirens, almost like they're happening again. I’m always on edge, always checking my surroundings, like where the exits are or who's behind me.
D018-D005_h020.options:

D018-D005_h021.question:
It's been about nine months since the accident, and honestly, things just haven't been right. I'm 53 now, and my wife, bless her heart, tries to help, but it's like I'm stuck. Every time I hear a screech of tires or even just see a flash of brake lights in my rearview, I get this gut-wrenching feeling, like I'm back in that moment, seeing the car swerve right in front of my bus. It’s not just a memory; it’s like it’s happening all over again. Sometimes, it’s so vivid, I actually 'see' the whole crash unfolding in front of me, even when I know I'm sitting in my living room. These aren't like other strange thoughts sometimes described by others; these are only and always about the accident.

I used to love taking our grandkids to the park, but now, even when they’re laughing and playing, I can't feel any joy. It’s like a switch got flipped off. I just feel this deep shame, like I could have done more, even though everyone says it wasn't my fault. And I’ve been so on edge. The other day, a fellow driver just asked me for a wrench, and I just exploded at him, yelling and cussing him out. I felt terrible afterward, but in the moment, I just couldn’t hold it in.
D018-D005_h021.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D018-D005_h022.question: It's been about seven months since… the incident. I keep reliving it, even in my sleep. D018-D005_h022.options:

D018-D005_h023.question: It's been a rough few months, nearly eight now, since that passenger jumped in front of my train. I  still hear the screech of the brakes, the thud. D018-D005_h025.question: It’s been over a year since the accident at the shipyard, but it feels like yesterday. Every night, I’m back there, reliving the explosion.
